children: New Zealand home prices slipped in September as higher living costs, a stagnant job market and global uncertainties continued to weigh on buying confidence, the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand (REINZ) said on Wednesday.
Seasonally adjusted median house prices fell 1% from August and were down 2.3% from a year earlier, indicating the usual spring lift in the market had yet to arrive, REINZ data showed.
National home sales fell 4.3% on the month and were down almost 11% year-on-year.
"Activity is continuing, but decisions are not being rushed," said REINZ Chief Executive Lizzy Ryley.
"Buyers are moving forward when the property, price and timing suit their circumstances, while many vendors recognise that achieving a sale may require patience."
Regionally, the South Island continued to outperform the North Island, supported by stronger employment and favourable agricultural conditions.
Ryley said conditions were expected to remain steady in the near term, with the potential for activity to pick up in the lead-up to summer, beginning in December.

Some vendors and buyers were also adopting a 'wait-and-see' approach ahead of the November national election, which is shaping up to be a tight contest between the ruling centre-right coalition and a Labour-led left bloc.
